elements.content: Grammar focus: Inverted 3rd Conditionals & Mixed Hypotheticals.

Core Rule: Invert past unreal conditions: Had + Subject + Past Participle , linked to complex modal result clauses ( would have + V3 , would + Base Verb , or might conceivably have + V3 ).

Pure 3rd Inversion — Had + S + V3 ..., S + would have + V3: Had liquidity frozen , three major lenders would have collapsed .
3rd -> Present Mixed — Had + S + V3 ..., S + would + Base: Had the central bank raised rates , inflation would be manageable today .
Modalized 3rd — Had + S + V3 ..., S + might conceivably have + V3: Had stimulus been delayed , recovery might conceivably have stalled .
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which sentence forms a correct inverted past counterfactual?
options: Had the board acted promptly, the breach would have been contained.
Had the board acted promptly, the breach was contained.

elements.content: 2. What word is inverted to the sentence-initial position in past unreal conditions?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

Had it not been for you, we would have failed.
Were it not for the rain, we would go.
Had she known, she would have called.
Should it prove false, we will withdraw.

Second grammar point of the lesson: Conditional Inversion in Economic Forecasting. Core Rule: Deploy inverted conditionals in economic forecasting: Had + S + V3 for historical counterfactuals, Were + S + to + Base for hypothetical forward-looking scenarios.
